mc.print.same_line.belief: Several print lines all show on one line.
mc.print.same_line.correct_model: Each print starts its own new line.

feedback.adults: Each print starts a new line.
feedback.kids: Every print gets its own line!

mc.order.any_order.belief: The computer can run lines in any order.
mc.order.any_order.correct_model: Lines run one by one, top to bottom.

feedback.adults: Python reads from the top down, like a recipe.
feedback.kids: Python goes from the top line to the bottom line.

mc.str.quotes_shown.correct_model: Quotes mark where text starts and ends; they are not shown.

feedback.adults: The quotes mark the text; print doesn't show them.
feedback.kids: The quotes are just the wrapping. They don't show up.

mc.str.quotes_shown.hint: Look closely at what print shows.

mc.str.text_is_evaluated.correct_model: Inside quotes everything is plain text, copied exactly.

feedback.adults: Inside quotes, Python doesn't do maths; it copies the text.
feedback.kids: Inside quotes, Python just copies the letters and numbers.

mc.str.no_digits_in_text.belief: Text can't contain digits or symbols.
mc.str.no_digits_in_text.correct_model: Text can hold any characters, digits and symbols too.

feedback.adults: Text can hold any characters, digits too.
feedback.kids: Text can have numbers in it. That's fine!

mc.str.no_digits_in_text.hint: Can a message contain a number?

mc.str.missing_quotes.belief: Words can be printed without quotes.
mc.str.missing_quotes.correct_model: Without quotes, Python reads a word as a name, not text.

feedback.adults: Without quotes, Python looks for a name instead of text.
feedback.kids: Put quotes around words so Python knows they are text.

mc.str.unclosed_quote.correct_model: Text needs an opening and a matching closing quote.

feedback.adults: Every opening quote needs a matching closing one.
feedback.kids: Quotes come in pairs: one at the start, one at the end.

mc.syn.case_insensitive.correct_model: Print and print are different names; capitals matter.

feedback.adults: Capitals matter: Print is not print.
feedback.kids: Python cares about big and small letters. Use print.

mc.syn.other_language.belief: Python uses the same symbols as other languages (semicolons, colons for values).
mc.syn.other_language.correct_model: Python has its own rules; it doesn't need semicolons and uses = to name values.

feedback.adults: Python has its own rules; that symbol isn't needed here.
feedback.kids: Python doesn't use that symbol here.

mc.syn.other_language.hint: What does the error message say?

mc.syn.natural_language.belief: Python understands English words and checks spelling.
mc.syn.natural_language.correct_model: Python only knows its own words; it never checks the spelling inside text.

feedback.adults: Python only knows its own words, like print, and doesn't check spelling inside text.
feedback.kids: Python only knows its own special words, like print.

mc.syn.natural_language.hint: Look back at the first example.

mc.gen.misread_goal.belief: Any change that runs is fine.
mc.gen.misread_goal.correct_model: The task asks for one exact result.

feedback.adults: Read the task again: it asks for an exact result.
feedback.kids: Read the task again. What should it show?

mc.var.name_vs_value.belief: A name without quotes prints the name itself (or a name in quotes prints its value).
mc.var.name_vs_value.correct_model: Without quotes it is a name and Python shows its value; in quotes it is text.

feedback.adults: Without quotes it's a name, so Python shows its value. In quotes it's just text.
feedback.kids: No quotes: Python shows what the name is stuck on. Quotes: it shows the word.

mc.var.name_vs_value.hint: Is it in quotes or not?

mc.var.prints_statement.belief: An assignment line shows something on screen.
mc.var.prints_statement.correct_model: Assignment only sticks a name on a value; only print shows anything.

feedback.adults: The first line sets the tag; only print shows anything.
feedback.kids: Making a variable doesn't show anything. Only print shows things.

mc.var.needs_declaration.belief: A variable must be set up or declared before =.
mc.var.needs_declaration.correct_model: In Python, the = line creates the name. No setup needed.

feedback.adults: In Python, using = creates the name. No setup needed.
feedback.kids: Using = makes the name. That's all you need!

mc.var.first_value_sticks.belief: A variable keeps its first value forever.
mc.var.first_value_sticks.correct_model: A new assignment moves the name to the new value.

feedback.adults: The newer line moves the tag to a new value.
feedback.kids: The tag moved! It's on the newest value now.

mc.var.first_value_sticks.hint: What does the later line do to the tag?

mc.var.holds_history.belief: A variable keeps every value it was ever given.
mc.var.holds_history.correct_model: A name points at one value at a time; a new assignment moves the name.

feedback.adults: A tag is on one value at a time, not a list of old ones.
feedback.kids: A tag can only be on one thing at a time.

mc.var.holds_history.hint: How many values can one tag be on?

mc.var.assign_adds.belief: Assigning again adds or joins the new value to the old one.
mc.var.assign_adds.correct_model: = moves the tag; it never adds or joins.

feedback.adults: = moves the tag; it doesn't add or join.
feedback.kids: = just moves the tag. Nothing gets added.

mc.var.assign_adds.hint: Is there anything here that adds?

mc.var.linked_names.belief: After b = a, b follows a forever.
mc.var.linked_names.correct_model: b = a sticks b on a's value at that moment; moving a later doesn't move b.

feedback.adults: b = a sticks b on a's value at that moment, not on a.
feedback.kids: b got a's value at that moment. Moving a later doesn't move b.

mc.var.linked_names.hint: Draw the tags after each line.

mc.var.quotes_around_name.belief: A variable name should go in quotes.
mc.var.quotes_around_name.correct_model: Quotes make text; a name is used without quotes.

feedback.adults: Quotes would make it text, not the variable.
feedback.kids: Quotes turn it into a word. Take them off to use the tag.

mc.var.cannot_print.correct_model: print can show any variable's value.

feedback.adults: print can show any variable's value.
feedback.kids: print can show what any tag is stuck on.

mc.var.cannot_print.hint: Look back at the first example.

mc.var.used_before_made.belief: A name can be used before the line that makes it.
mc.var.used_before_made.correct_model: Lines run top to bottom, so a name must be made before it's used.

feedback.adults: Lines run top to bottom, so the name must exist before it's used.
feedback.kids: Python reads top to bottom. Make the tag first, then use it.

mc.var.bypasses_variable.belief: Typing the text directly is the same as using the variable.
mc.var.bypasses_variable.correct_model: The task asks you to use the variable's name inside print.

feedback.adults: Use the variable's name inside print, not the text itself.
feedback.kids: Use the tag's name inside print.

mc.err.points_to_cause.belief: The error is always somewhere other than the line it names.
mc.err.points_to_cause.correct_model: Read the error: it names the line and the name it couldn't find.

feedback.adults: Read the error: it names the exact line and name.
feedback.kids: The error message tells you which line. Read it!

mc.err.points_to_cause.hint: Which line does the error name?
